assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is LLM tool-use engineering: schema design, ReAct loops, tool selection, code sandboxes, fine-tuning data, error handling
practitioner has access to at least one capable LLM API and can deploy containerized compute
evaluation is accuracy-centric (tool selection, argument correctness) unless project overrides
exclusions: first-stage retrieval and embedding model training internals
RAG pipeline construction beyond tool-result injection
LLM pre-training and base model selection
human-computer interaction and UX design of tool-calling interfaces

competency_questions.question: What tool schema fields are required for an LLM to reliably populate arguments without hallucination?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCHEMA_DESIGN defines required fields and description guidelines

competency_questions.question: How is tool-use quality measured and what metrics distinguish argument errors from routing errors?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOOL_EVAL defines selection accuracy, argument correctness, and hallucinated call rate

competency_questions.question: How does the ReAct loop coordinate reasoning and tool execution across multiple steps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REACT_LOOP and TOOL_SELECTION define loop mechanics and routing

competency_questions.question: How are multi-step tool plans constructed and how are dependencies between subtasks managed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLANNING defines decomposition, dependency graph, and branching

competency_questions.question: How are independent tool calls parallelized and how are partial failures handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARALLEL_CALLS and ERROR_HANDLING define fan-out and failure aggregation

competency_questions.question: What latency and cost optimization strategies apply to tool-augmented inference pipelines?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LATENCY_COST and PARALLEL_CALLS define caching, batching, and tier selection

competency_questions.question: How are tool errors classified and recovered from without exposing incorrect answers to users?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ERROR_HANDLING and FALLBACK_DEGRADE define classification and recovery paths

competency_questions.question: How is tool-use fine-tuning data generated and what prevents benchmark contamination?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOOL_FINETUNE and TOOLFORMER_SELF_SUP define data generation and contamination controls

competency_questions.question: How are code execution sandboxes secured and what trust boundaries govern tool execution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODE_EXEC and TRUST_BOUNDARY define isolation, resource limits, and permission model

competency_questions.question: How is agent memory structured and what prevents stale or poisoned memory from corrupting future responses?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEMORY_TOOLS defines store types and TRUST_BOUNDARY defines write sanitization

competency_questions.question: How do multi-agent pipelines coordinate tool handoffs and propagate errors across agent boundaries?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTI_AGENT_TOOLS defines handoff contracts and error propagation

competency_questions.question: How is tool-use pipeline health monitored and how quickly are regressions detected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OBSERVABILITY defines tracing, alerting, and regression detection SLA

competency_questions.question: How does schema versioning prevent breaking changes from invalidating deployed fine-tuned models?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCHEMA_VERSIONING defines compatibility rules and migration path

glossary.definition: JSON or OpenAPI specification of a callable tool's name, parameters, types, and descriptions
Reason+Act interleaved agent loop (Yao et al. 2022) alternating thought traces and tool actions
LLM-generated structured request to invoke a registered tool with specific arguments
Self-supervised method (Schick et al. 2023) using perplexity reduction to filter LLM-generated tool calls into training data
Criterion rejecting tool calls that do not reduce language model perplexity on the surrounding context
Access control model granting tool invocation rights based on task-scoped capability tokens rather than global ACLs
Adversarial technique embedding instructions in user-controlled input to hijack LLM behavior including tool argument generation
Explicit schema for data passed between agents in a multi-agent pipeline, including required fields and error status
Maximum token allocation for tool schemas, results, and examples within a model's context window

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for tool-use and function-calling work units in absence of supplied datasets; grounded in Yao et al. 2022 (ReAct), Schick et al. 2023 (Toolformer), and Russell & Norvig AIMA planning
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Yao et al. 2022 ReAct; Schick et al. 2023 Toolformer; Russell & Norvig AIMA 4th ed.
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors informed by key literature

nodes.definition: Design JSON/OpenAPI tool schemas (name, description, parameter types, required fields) that LLMs parse reliably without hallucinating arguments.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new LLM release or API surface change

pros.claim: Precise schemas reduce hallucinated argument names and wrong types
pros.example: strict enum on 'action' param cuts invalid calls by 40% in practice

pros.claim: Self-documenting descriptions guide tool selection
pros.example: docstring 'Use this to search products, not orders' cuts routing errors

cons.claim: Overly strict schemas block valid edge-case inputs
cons.example: required lat/lon fails for city-name-only queries

cons.claim: Long descriptions consume context budget
cons.example: 50-tool schema set can exhaust 4K tokens before the user query

failure_modes: ambiguous parameter names causing hallucinated values
missing required-vs-optional distinction
schema version drift from underlying API
acceptance_tests: LLM correctly populates all required fields on 10 diverse golden prompts
no undefined property errors when schema validated against JSON Schema draft-07
revisit_triggers: underlying API signature changes
new LLM model shows different schema parsing behavior

nodes.definition: Decide which tool(s) to invoke given a user request; includes single-tool dispatch, multi-tool planning, and no-tool (direct answer) routing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tools deployed or query distribution shifts

pros.claim: Correct routing eliminates wasted API calls and latency
pros.example: routing to calculator instead of LLM for arithmetic saves 2s round-trip

pros.claim: No-tool path preserves context when answer is in model weights
pros.example: avoids unnecessary search for factual queries the model knows reliably

cons.claim: Ambiguous requests cause mis-routing with silent failures
cons.example: 'book a table' might route to calendar or restaurant tool

cons.claim: Multi-tool routing amplifies error compounding across steps
cons.example: error in step-1 tool propagates to steps 2-3 without recovery

failure_modes: routing to wrong tool silently returns plausible-but-wrong result
model invokes tool when direct answer is better (tool overuse)
parallel tool calls with ordering dependencies
acceptance_tests: routing evaluation on 50-query golden set achieves >=90% correct tool selection
no-tool path invoked for >=80% of greetings/simple factual queries in test set
revisit_triggers: new tool added to registry
traffic distribution shifts to new request type

nodes.definition: Implement the Reason+Act interleaved loop (Yao et al. 2022): model emits thought traces, then tool calls, then observes results, iterating until task complete.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new model or task type requiring loop redesign

pros.claim: Interleaved reasoning improves multi-step accuracy over single-pass
pros.example: ReAct outperforms CoT-only on HotpotQA by reducing hallucinated paths

pros.claim: Thought traces enable post-hoc debugging and interpretability
pros.example: operators can audit why a tool was called via the thought log

cons.claim: Loop overhead multiplies latency per step
cons.example: 5-step loop at 1s/step adds 5s vs sub-second direct answer

cons.claim: Runaway loops exhaust token budget without termination
cons.example: missing stop condition leads to infinite thought-action cycles

failure_modes: infinite loop without convergence criterion
observation injection hallucinated instead of actual API result
thought trace diverges from actual action taken
acceptance_tests: loop terminates within configured max_iterations on all golden tasks
thought content references actual observation text, not hallucinated content
revisit_triggers: new model with different instruction-following behavior for thought format
task complexity distribution shifts requiring more or fewer steps

nodes.definition: Execute multiple independent tool calls in a single model turn to reduce total latency; manage fan-out, result aggregation, and partial failure handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: executor infrastructure change or new tool dependency patterns

pros.claim: Eliminates sequential latency for independent sub-tasks
pros.example: parallel web search + calculator cuts 2-step latency by ~50%

pros.claim: Enables richer answers by gathering multiple data sources simultaneously
pros.example: weather+news+calendar fetched in one turn for morning briefing

cons.claim: Partial failures require robust aggregation logic
cons.example: one tool timeout must not block returning the other 3 results

cons.claim: LLM must correctly identify independence; false independence causes data races
cons.example: reading then writing same resource in parallel corrupts state

failure_modes: false independence assumption causing race conditions
missing partial-failure propagation hiding errors in final answer
context window overflow from too many concurrent results
acceptance_tests: parallel execution completes at most max(individual_latencies) on independent golden pairs
partial failure in one call does not crash entire response
revisit_triggers: new model with different parallel call format
executor timeout policy change

nodes.definition: Detect, classify, and recover from tool errors: transient API failures (retry with backoff), argument errors (re-prompt with schema hint), permission errors (escalate or skip), and semantic failures (reformulate).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool class or external API policy change

pros.claim: Retry with backoff recovers from transient failures transparently
pros.example: 3-retry exponential backoff handles 95% of 429/503 tool errors

pros.claim: Structured error feedback enables argument self-correction
pros.example: returning schema diff on malformed call allows model to fix params in next turn

cons.claim: Aggressive retry amplifies rate-limiting and increases cost
cons.example: retrying a 429 too fast triggers longer cooldowns

cons.claim: Silent error swallowing produces confidently wrong answers
cons.example: catching all exceptions and returning empty result hides data gaps

failure_modes: retry storm under sustained API outage
argument error misclassified as transient → infinite retry loop
permission error escalation path undefined → silent data gap
acceptance_tests: all golden transient error scenarios resolve within 3 retries
argument errors return schema-informed hint to LLM within one turn
permission errors escalate or degrade gracefully without exception crash
revisit_triggers: new tool added with unique error codes
rate limit policy changes on external API

nodes.definition: Curate, format, and quality-filter SFT/RLHF data for teaching LLMs to call tools correctly: schema adherence, argument generation, and multi-turn conversation with tool results.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: schema or tool registry change requiring data refresh

pros.claim: Dedicated tool-call data dramatically improves schema adherence
pros.example: Toolformer (Schick 2023) showed self-supervised tool data boosts API use accuracy

pros.claim: Negative examples teach the model when NOT to call tools
pros.example: contrapositive examples cut tool overuse by ~30% in ablation studies

cons.claim: Synthetic tool-call data can overfit to data-generator patterns
cons.example: model learns to match simulator format, fails on real API quirks

cons.claim: Contamination with evaluation tasks inflates benchmark scores
cons.example: Goodhart: model memorizes golden tool sequences rather than generalizing

failure_modes: benchmark contamination from eval tasks in training split
format mismatch between training tool JSON and inference schema
distributional shift: training on simple single-tool, inference needs multi-tool
acceptance_tests: zero tool-call format errors on held-out schema set
eval split contains no queries from training demonstrations
dataset card lists negative-example fraction and source policy
revisit_triggers: schema updated post-training requiring re-curate
new tool class added requiring new demonstration templates

nodes.definition: Provision and operate secure sandboxed environments for LLM-generated code execution: isolation, resource limits, timeout enforcement, output capture, and safe result return.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new language runtime or security advisory

pros.claim: Sandboxed execution enables verified numerical/algorithmic results
pros.example: code interpreter pattern achieves near-perfect arithmetic vs pure LLM

pros.claim: Resource limits prevent runaway code from consuming infra
pros.example: CPU/memory caps kill infinite-loop code within configured timeout

cons.claim: Container cold-start latency adds hundreds of ms per execution
cons.example: cold Docker start adds 300-800ms on first invocation

cons.claim: Restrictive allowlists break legitimate library use cases
cons.example: blocking 'requests' prevents valid HTTP tasks in sandbox

failure_modes: sandbox escape via symlink or path traversal in generated code
resource limit bypass via forked processes evading per-PID accounting
output truncation silently losing part of execution result
acceptance_tests: generated malicious code attempt is isolated and logged without host impact
execution respects CPU/memory/time limits on golden stress tests
all output returned intact for 10KB+ output golden cases
revisit_triggers: new language runtime added to sandbox
security advisory for container runtime

nodes.definition: Format and inject tool call results back into the LLM context window: truncation policy, citation markers, result deduplication, and relevance filtering before next model forward pass.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new model context window or result format change

pros.claim: Structured result injection reduces model confusion from noisy raw output
pros.example: stripping HTML boilerplate from search results improves answer accuracy

pros.claim: Citation anchors enable verifiable references in final answer
pros.example: [SRC:3] anchor lets downstream system map claim to source document

cons.claim: Aggressive truncation discards relevant content at boundaries
cons.example: cutting search result at 500 tokens loses the key sentence in paragraph 4

cons.claim: Injecting all parallel results overwhelms context for large fan-out
cons.example: 20 tool results at 1K tokens each exhausts 20K context budget

failure_modes: truncation at wrong boundary loses critical information
citation anchor desynchronization between injected block and final answer
deduplication removes structurally different but semantically similar results incorrectly
acceptance_tests: truncated result summaries pass human review for completeness on golden set
citation anchors resolve correctly in final answer for all golden multi-source queries
revisit_triggers: context window size changes with new model
tool result format changes from upstream API

nodes.definition: Decompose complex tasks into ordered subtask-tool sequences before execution; manage dependencies, intermediate state, and conditional branching between tool calls (Russell & Norvig AIMA planning).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool class or task complexity distribution change

pros.claim: Upfront planning avoids dead-end execution paths
pros.example: planning reveals missing permissions before 5-step execution starts

pros.claim: Dependency graph enables parallelization of independent subtasks
pros.example: parallel branches reduce total wall time for complex tasks

cons.claim: Planning overhead adds a full model forward pass before any execution
cons.example: up-front plan costs ~1s before first tool call

cons.claim: Brittle plans fail when early tool results invalidate assumptions
cons.example: plan assuming search returns N results fails when API returns 0

failure_modes: over-specified plan too brittle for dynamic tool outputs
under-specified plan creates ambiguous intermediate state handoffs
circular dependency in subtask graph causing deadlock
acceptance_tests: planner produces valid dependency-ordered subtask list for 10 golden complex tasks
plan adapts correctly when first-step tool returns unexpected result format
revisit_triggers: new tool type with unknown dependency patterns
task complexity distribution shifts

nodes.definition: Measure LLM tool-use quality: correct tool selection rate, argument accuracy, task completion, hallucinated call rate, and multi-step success vs oracle baselines.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool class or benchmark contamination detected

pros.claim: Quantitative metrics expose argument-level failure modes invisible to end-to-end task eval
pros.example: argument accuracy of 70% despite 90% task success reveals fragile luck-based paths

pros.claim: Held-out golden set prevents Goodhart overfitting to training distribution
pros.example: separate eval from training data preserves metric validity

cons.claim: Golden set quickly saturates — model memorizes evaluation queries
cons.example: 50-query golden set exhausted after 3 training iterations in practice

cons.claim: Task completion as proxy metric masks wrong tool paths that accidentally succeed
cons.example: wrong tool + correct downstream reasoning accidentally passes task check

failure_modes: eval set contamination in training data
metric gaming via shortcut answers that pass task check
oracle sequence mismatch when API schema updates
acceptance_tests: argument accuracy computed correctly on 10 golden multi-argument calls
hallucinated call rate measured on 20 no-tool-needed queries
revisit_triggers: evaluation golden set refreshed
new tool class requires new eval metrics

nodes.definition: Manage backward-compatible schema evolution: version fields, deprecation notices, additive-only changes, and migration paths for deployed LLMs trained on older schema versions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: underlying API breaking change or new LLM deployment

pros.claim: Additive-only changes keep deployed models operational without retraining
pros.example: adding optional parameter is transparent to models trained on v1 schema

pros.claim: Version field in schema enables conditional logic in tool dispatch layer
pros.example: dispatcher routes v1 vs v2 clients to correct handler

cons.claim: Breaking changes require coordinated retraining and deployment
cons.example: renaming required parameter forces full SFT data refresh and model redeploy

cons.claim: Accumulation of deprecated fields bloats schema context consumption
cons.example: 15 deprecated params still in schema waste 200 tokens of context per call

failure_modes: silent breaking change invalidates trained models without version bump
accumulated deprecated fields bloating context
version field mismatch between training schema and inference schema
acceptance_tests: breaking change detected by compatibility test before merge
deprecated fields removed from active schema within 2 major versions
revisit_triggers: underlying API breaking change forces emergency migration
new LLM with different schema parsing behavior

nodes.definition: Design and integrate tool-accessible memory stores (short-term scratchpad, long-term vector/KV store, episodic log) enabling agents to persist and retrieve state across multi-turn sessions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: memory store schema or LLM context window change

pros.claim: Persistent memory enables coherent multi-session agents without context replay
pros.example: agent retrieves past user preference without re-reading full history

pros.claim: Episodic log enables diagnostic replay of agent execution paths
pros.example: log-based replay traces root cause of multi-step failure

cons.claim: Stale memory causes contradictory behavior when world state changes
cons.example: cached user preference overrides new explicit instruction

cons.claim: Memory retrieval latency adds per-turn overhead
cons.example: vector store recall adds 50-200ms per turn on hosted indices

failure_modes: stale memory overriding current instruction
memory poisoning via adversarial tool output injected into store
retrieval returning irrelevant entries that dilute context
acceptance_tests: memory write followed by retrieval returns consistent value within same session
stale entry eviction policy tested against golden staleness scenarios
revisit_triggers: memory store schema change
new model with longer context making memory less critical

nodes.definition: Define and enforce which tools an agent may call, with what arguments, under which user authorization levels; implement capability-based permission checks before execution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool class or security policy change

pros.claim: Capability-based permissions contain blast radius of compromised agent
pros.example: agent with write-access scope limited to user's own files cannot exfiltrate global data

pros.claim: Audit trail enables post-incident forensic analysis
pros.example: permission log shows exact tool+argument that caused unauthorized action

cons.claim: Over-permissioning nullifies security boundary
cons.example: agent with admin tool access in production can destroy any resource

cons.claim: Under-permissioning causes legitimate task failures requiring manual escalation
cons.example: agent denied read-file permission cannot complete code review task

failure_modes: privilege escalation via tool chaining (A reads secret, B exfiltrates it)
TOCTOU race between permission check and execution
permission policy not versioned with schema causing stale grants
acceptance_tests: privilege escalation via multi-tool chain blocked on golden attack scenarios
permission audit log entries present for all denied and approved tool calls
revisit_triggers: new tool class with new permission scope
security policy update

nodes.definition: Design system and few-shot prompt templates that convey available tool schemas, usage instructions, and worked examples to the LLM without consuming excessive context budget.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new model release or schema version update

pros.claim: Few-shot tool examples improve schema adherence without fine-tuning
pros.example: 3 examples cut malformed call rate by 35% on zero-shot capable models

pros.claim: Modular template enables tool subset injection per task type
pros.example: inject only search+calc tools for math queries, saving 500 context tokens

cons.claim: Large few-shot sets consume context budget needed for long conversations
cons.example: 8 examples at 200 tokens each = 1600 tokens of non-task content

cons.claim: Stale few-shot examples demonstrate deprecated schema format
cons.example: example showing v1 schema confuses model when v2 is active

failure_modes: few-shot examples with wrong schema format teaching incorrect patterns
template injecting all tools regardless of task wasting context
instruction ambiguity causing model to conflate tool descriptions
acceptance_tests: system prompt renders under 20% of context window for target model
few-shot examples all use current schema version
revisit_triggers: new model with different instruction format
schema version update

nodes.definition: Profile and optimize end-to-end latency and API cost of tool-augmented inference: caching tool results, batching calls, model tier selection per task step, and budget-aware loop termination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: provider pricing change or new model tier

pros.claim: Result caching eliminates redundant identical tool calls across sessions
pros.example: deterministic search query cached for 60s cuts duplicate call cost by 40%

pros.claim: Model tier selection (small vs large per step) reduces inference cost without quality loss
pros.example: routing arithmetic to small model saves 10x cost per step

cons.claim: Aggressive caching returns stale results for dynamic data
cons.example: cached weather result from 1 hour ago returns wrong current conditions

cons.claim: Budget-aware early termination may cut loop before finding optimal answer
cons.example: terminating at step 3 of 5 due to budget misses the critical 4th search

failure_modes: cache invalidation failure returning stale data confidently
budget termination silently truncating multi-step reasoning
cost model outdated after provider pricing change
acceptance_tests: cache-hit results match live results for deterministic golden queries
budget-terminated responses include explicit 'incomplete' flag in output
revisit_triggers: provider pricing change
new model tier with different cost profile

nodes.definition: Define and implement fallback behaviors when tools are unavailable or fail persistently: partial answers with uncertainty markers, alternative tool substitution, and graceful degradation to model-only response.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool without fallback or monitoring change

pros.claim: Graceful degradation maintains partial utility during tool outages
pros.example: returning model-only answer with caveat better than hard failure

pros.claim: Fallback logging enables root cause analysis and tool reliability tracking
pros.example: fallback events drive SLA review for unreliable tools

cons.claim: Model-only fallback can produce confident hallucinations when tool data is needed
cons.example: without search tool, model fabricates current stock price

cons.claim: Over-reliance on fallback masks persistent tool failures needing remediation
cons.example: fallback prevents alert triggering for a tool degraded for days

failure_modes: confident hallucination in model-only fallback for factual queries
fallback masking persistent tool failure from monitoring
alternative tool substitution introducing different data format without adaptation
acceptance_tests: fallback response includes explicit uncertainty marker for all tool-dependent queries
fallback events logged to monitoring with tool name and failure count
revisit_triggers: new tool with no designated fallback
monitoring stack change

nodes.definition: Apply Toolformer-style (Schick et al. 2023) self-supervised approach: LLM generates candidate tool calls, executes them, filters by perplexity reduction, and uses accepted calls as supervised training signal.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool API or task domain requiring data refresh

pros.claim: Scales tool-call data generation without expensive human annotation
pros.example: Toolformer generated 100K+ valid tool calls across calculator, search, wiki APIs

pros.claim: Perplexity filter ensures only helpful tool calls enter training data
pros.example: calls that don't reduce perplexity discarded, maintaining signal quality

cons.claim: Perplexity filter biased toward frequent patterns; rare but valid calls underrepresented
cons.example: low-frequency edge-case tool calls systematically rejected by perplexity criterion

cons.claim: Self-generated data can entrench model's existing tool-use biases
cons.example: model avoids tools it initially dislikes, creating circular training signal

failure_modes: perplexity filter discarding rare but critical tool use patterns
circular bias amplification through self-generated training data
generation cost exceeding annotation cost for rare tool domains
acceptance_tests: accepted call rate matches expected ~10-20% filter yield on golden candidate set
perplexity reduction verified positive for all accepted examples
revisit_triggers: perplexity filter threshold tuned for new task domain
new tool API with no prior LLM familiarity

nodes.definition: Coordinate tool calls across multiple specialized agents: define handoff contracts, result passing formats, error propagation protocols, and shared tool state management in multi-agent pipelines.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new agent added or shared state schema change

pros.claim: Specialist agents outperform a single generalist on narrow tool domains
pros.example: search-specialist agent + code-specialist agent beats monolithic agent on HotpotQA + coding benchmark

pros.claim: Explicit handoff contracts enable independent agent versioning and replacement
pros.example: replacing search agent v1 with v2 without retraining code agent

cons.claim: Handoff latency compounds across agent chain
cons.example: 4-agent chain with 500ms per handoff adds 2s fixed overhead

cons.claim: Error propagation ambiguity in multi-agent chains causes silent failures
cons.example: agent B receives malformed result from A without error signal, proceeds with wrong data

failure_modes: silent error propagation between agents
shared state write conflicts when two agents update concurrently
handoff schema mismatch between independently versioned agents
acceptance_tests: handoff result passes schema validation at each agent boundary
concurrent write conflicts resolved by optimistic locking on golden contention scenarios
revisit_triggers: new agent added to pipeline
shared state store schema change

nodes.definition: Instrument tool-augmented inference pipelines with distributed tracing, structured logging of tool calls/results/latencies, anomaly detection, and dashboards for per-tool reliability and cost metrics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool without instrumentation or storage policy change

pros.claim: Distributed tracing correlates tool failures to user experience degradation
pros.example: P99 latency spike in search tool traced to upstream index rebuild

pros.claim: Per-tool error rate alerting catches silent regressions before user reports
pros.example: error rate alert fires within 5 min of tool API deprecation

cons.claim: Trace data volume can exceed storage budget for high-volume deployments
cons.example: 1M traces/day at 10KB each = 10GB/day raw trace storage

cons.claim: Sampling reduces trace volume but loses rare failure events
cons.example: 1% sampling misses rare but critical permission denial traces

failure_modes: sampling rate too low to catch rare failure modes
trace schema mismatch between service versions breaking dashboard queries
alert threshold miscalibrated causing alert fatigue or missed incidents
acceptance_tests: all tool call boundaries emit trace span with tool name, latency, and status
error rate alert fires within 10 minutes of injected golden failure scenario
revisit_triggers: new tool added without trace instrumentation
storage budget change requiring sampling adjustment

nodes.definition: Maintain a versioned registry of available tools with metadata (schema version, owner, SLA, cost tier, capability tags) enabling dynamic tool discovery and selection at runtime.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: infrastructure change or capability taxonomy update

pros.claim: Dynamic tool discovery allows agent to use newly deployed tools without code change
pros.example: new translation tool auto-discovered and used by routing layer within minutes of registration

pros.claim: SLA metadata enables cost- and reliability-aware tool selection
pros.example: routing avoids P99>2s tool for latency-sensitive tasks based on SLA field

cons.claim: Registry becomes single point of failure if tools depend on it at call time
cons.example: registry outage blocks all tool selection, degrading every agent

cons.claim: Stale registry entries for deprecated tools cause routing to dead endpoints
cons.example: deprecated tool still in registry causes 404 errors until TTL expires

failure_modes: registry outage cascading to agent tool selection failure
stale entries routing to deprecated tool endpoints
capability tag inconsistency causing incorrect semantic routing
acceptance_tests: newly registered tool discoverable by routing layer within 60s of registration
deprecated tool entries removed from registry within configured TTL
revisit_triggers: tool registry infrastructure change
new capability taxonomy requiring re-tagging

nodes.definition: Validate and sanitize LLM-generated tool arguments before execution: type checking, range validation, injection prevention, and argument coercion to canonical form.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new tool argument types or injection pattern update

pros.claim: Schema-based validation catches type errors before execution
pros.example: string-to-int coercion failure caught before DB query prevents silent integer overflow

pros.claim: Injection prevention blocks prompt injection via tool argument
pros.example: blocklist prevents </tool_call> injection in user-controlled string argument

cons.claim: Over-zealous sanitization rejects valid inputs with special characters
cons.example: sanitizer strips legitimate code snippet argument for code-execution tool

cons.claim: Validation adds per-call latency overhead on hot paths
cons.example: 200ms validation on 50ms tool call adds 400% overhead

failure_modes: prompt injection via LLM-controlled argument reaching execution layer
type coercion silently changing argument semantics (str '0' to int 0 to bool False)
validation bypass via nested JSON structure exploiting schema dereferencing
acceptance_tests: all 10 golden injection patterns blocked at validation layer without exception
validated arguments type-match schema on 100 diverse golden calls
revisit_triggers: new tool with novel argument types requiring new validation rules
injection pattern library update

conflict_axes.name: schema_strictness_vs_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Strict schemas reduce hallucinated arguments but reject valid edge-case inputs; flexible schemas accept more but increase argument error rate.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: SCHEMA_DESIGN strict → ARGUMENT_VALIDATION rejects valid inputs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use strict types with optional fields for edge cases; never make user-controlled strings enum-constrained

conflict_axes.name: tool_call_accuracy_vs_latency
conflict_axes.description: More ReAct loop steps improve answer quality but multiply latency; fewer steps reduce latency but risk incomplete reasoning.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tier tasks by complexity; assign step budget per tier; surface incomplete-flag when terminated early

conflict_axes.name: tool_overuse_vs_underuse
conflict_axes.description: Models fine-tuned heavily on tool data may call tools when direct answers suffice; lightly tuned models may avoid tools when needed.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: include no-tool negative examples in training data; evaluate no-tool rate explicitly

conflict_axes.name: cache_freshness_vs_cost
conflict_axes.description: Longer cache TTLs reduce tool call cost but increase staleness risk for dynamic data sources.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: LATENCY_COST↓ via longer TTL → stale data risk↑
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag tools as static/dynamic; apply zero TTL to dynamic tools regardless of cost pressure

conflict_axes.name: schema_stability_vs_evolution
conflict_axes.description: Frequent schema updates improve expressiveness but break fine-tuned models and invalidate training data.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: SCHEMA_VERSIONING breaking changes → TOOL_FINETUNE data refresh required
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: additive-only changes between training runs; coordinate breaking changes with retraining milestone

conflict_axes.name: security_strictness_vs_agent_capability
conflict_axes.description: Tight permission boundaries prevent misuse but may block legitimate complex multi-step agent tasks.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: TRUST_BOUNDARY restrictive → PLANNING cannot execute required tool chain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grant least-privilege per task type; introduce elevated-permission audit path for complex tasks

conflict_axes.name: self_supervised_data_scale_vs_quality
conflict_axes.description: Perplexity filter in Toolformer-style generation scales cheaply but filters rare valid patterns; human annotation is expensive but covers edge cases.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: TOOLFORMER_SELF_SUP filters rare calls → TOOL_FINETUNE underrepresents edge cases
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: supplement self-supervised data with targeted human annotations for low-frequency high-value tool patterns

conflict_axes.name: parallel_execution_vs_consistency
conflict_axes.description: Parallel tool calls reduce latency but risk data races when calls have hidden state dependencies.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: PARALLEL_CALLS independence assumption → PLANNING must verify true independence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require planner to explicitly assert independence before fan-out; default to sequential if uncertain

conflict_axes.name: context_richness_vs_budget
conflict_axes.description: Injecting full tool results and few-shot examples improves answer quality but consumes context window needed for task content.
conflict_axes.tension_direction: CONTEXT_INJECTION full results + PROMPT_TEMPLATES few-shot → context budget exhaustion
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: budget context allocation: reserve 60% for task/history, 20% for tool results, 20% for system/templates

conflict_axes.name: multi_agent_isolation_vs_coordination_overhead
conflict_axes.description: Strict agent isolation prevents error propagation but increases coordination latency and handoff complexity.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: isolate error boundaries but share read-only state; minimize handoff payload to essential fields only

edge_cases.description: Tool returns valid JSON but semantically wrong value (e.g., stale stock price from 2020)
edge_cases.mitigation: timestamp-validate tool results; warn on stale data flag

edge_cases.description: LLM generates syntactically valid but semantically nonsensical argument (e.g., latitude=999)
edge_cases.mitigation: add semantic range validators beyond JSON schema type checks

edge_cases.description: Tool call invoked with user-controlled string containing prompt injection
edge_cases.mitigation: blocklist injection patterns; never interpolate user strings into system tool argument fields

edge_cases.description: ReAct loop converges on wrong answer confidently within max_iterations
edge_cases.mitigation: add external verifier tool call at final step for high-stakes tasks

edge_cases.description: Parallel tool calls with hidden temporal dependency cause race condition
edge_cases.mitigation: require planner to prove independence; add write-after-read guard in executor

edge_cases.description: Schema version mismatch: model trained on v1 receives v2 schema at inference
edge_cases.mitigation: version gate in registry returns schema version matching model training version

edge_cases.description: Memory store poisoning: malicious tool output injected into persistent memory
edge_cases.mitigation: validate and sanitize all memory writes; scope memory entries to session and user

edge_cases.description: Code sandbox escape via generated code exploiting container runtime vulnerability
edge_cases.mitigation: keep container runtime patched; apply seccomp/apparmor profiles; network-isolated sandbox

edge_cases.description: Tool registry outage cascades to agent complete inability to select tools
edge_cases.mitigation: cache last-known registry snapshot locally; fallback to cached schema on registry unavailability

edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination: evaluation tool-call sequences appear in Toolformer training data
edge_cases.mitigation: deduplicate training data against eval golden set by query hash before filtering

edge_cases.description: Multi-agent handoff delivers partial result from failed upstream agent without error signal
edge_cases.mitigation: require explicit status field in all handoff packets; reject partial results without error annotation

edge_cases.description: Perplexity filter in self-supervised generation systematically rejects low-frequency but critical tool calls
edge_cases.mitigation: supplement perplexity-filtered data with targeted human demonstrations for underrepresented tool patterns

workflow.name: Define tool schemas and capability taxonomy
workflow.action: Author JSON schemas for all tools; register with capability tags and SLA metadata
workflow.gate: all required fields documented; schema passes JSON Schema draft-07 validation

workflow.name: Design prompt templates and few-shot examples
workflow.action: Create system prompt templates and curate minimal few-shot tool-call examples
workflow.output: prompt template library with token budget analysis
workflow.gate: templates render under 20% of context window for target model

workflow.name: Implement argument validation and trust boundaries
workflow.action: Build schema-derived validators; define permission policy per tool and user tier
workflow.gate: golden injection attempts blocked; permission audit log active

workflow.name: Provision code execution sandbox
workflow.action: Deploy containerized sandbox with resource limits, seccomp profile, and network isolation
workflow.output: sandboxed execution environment with timeout enforcement
workflow.gate: golden malicious code isolated without host impact

workflow.name: Implement ReAct loop and planning layer
workflow.action: Build interleaved thought-action loop; implement task decomposition planner
workflow.output: working ReAct loop with configurable max_iterations and task planner
workflow.gate: loop terminates on all golden tasks; planner produces valid dependency-ordered plan

workflow.name: Enable parallel execution and context injection
workflow.action: Implement fan-out executor; build result formatter with truncation and citation policy
workflow.output: parallel call executor + context injection module
workflow.gate: parallel golden pairs complete at max(individual_latencies); partial failures handled

workflow.name: Add error handling, fallback, and memory tools
workflow.action: Implement retry/backoff; define fallback policy; integrate memory store read/write tools
workflow.output: error classification module + fallback policy + memory tool integrations
workflow.gate: transient errors recover within 3 retries; fallback responses include uncertainty marker

workflow.name: Curate and generate tool-use fine-tuning data
workflow.action: Generate self-supervised tool-call data via perplexity filtering; supplement with human demos; deduplicate against eval set
workflow.output: cleaned SFT dataset with data card
workflow.gate: zero format errors on held-out schema; eval contamination check passes

workflow.name: Fine-tune and evaluate tool-use model
workflow.action: Run SFT on tool-use dataset; evaluate tool selection accuracy, argument correctness, and hallucinated call rate
workflow.gate: >=90% tool selection accuracy on golden set; hallucinated call rate <=10%

workflow.name: Instrument observability and run multi-agent integration
workflow.action: Deploy distributed tracing; integrate specialist agents with handoff contracts; load test multi-agent pipeline
workflow.output: instrumented pipeline with per-tool dashboards + multi-agent integration test results
workflow.gate: latency SLA met at P99; error rate alert fires within 10 min of injected failure

workflow.name: Optimize latency and cost; manage schema versioning
workflow.action: Profile hot paths; implement result caching with TTL policy; establish schema version governance
workflow.gate: P50 latency meets SLA target; deprecated fields removed within 2 versions

workflow.name: Production readiness review and rollout
workflow.action: Security review of permission policies; final eval on holdout set; canary rollout with error rate monitoring
workflow.output: security sign-off + production readiness report + rollout plan
workflow.gate: all critical acceptance tests pass; security review complete; canary error rate within baseline

dominance_rules.condition: trust boundary or argument validation check conflicts with latency target
dominance_rules.rationale: Privilege escalation or injection attack via tool argument is unacceptable regardless of latency SLA

dominance_rules.rule: Schema-derived validation dominates LLM-generated argument trust
dominance_rules.condition: LLM-generated argument conflicts with schema type or range constraints
dominance_rules.rationale: LLM arguments must never be trusted without validation; execution-layer errors are harder to debug than input rejection

dominance_rules.rule: Eval contamination prevention dominates data scale
dominance_rules.condition: self-supervised training data overlaps with evaluation golden set
dominance_rules.rationale: Contaminated eval metrics are misleading; scale without clean eval is worthless

dominance_rules.rule: Breaking schema change blocks training run
dominance_rules.condition: schema version bump introduces breaking change while training data refresh is incomplete
dominance_rules.rationale: Training on stale schema produces model that fails at inference on updated schema; always complete data refresh before training

dominance_rules.rule: Sandbox isolation dominates code execution capability
dominance_rules.condition: generated code requires capability that would require disabling sandbox
dominance_rules.rationale: Sandbox escape risk outweighs any single task capability gain; fail the task, do not weaken isolation

dominance_rules.condition: tool error is semantic (wrong data) rather than transient
dominance_rules.rationale: Silently continuing with wrong data produces confidently wrong answers; explicit error + caveat is always safer than silent fallback

dominance_rules.rule: Tool selection accuracy dominates loop efficiency
dominance_rules.condition: routing to cheaper/faster tool produces wrong result type
dominance_rules.rationale: Fast wrong answer is worse than slow correct answer; never sacrifice routing accuracy for cost

dominance_rules.rule: Schema documentation completeness dominates prompt brevity
dominance_rules.condition: shortening tool description to save context tokens introduces ambiguity
dominance_rules.rationale: Ambiguous schema descriptions cause systematic argument errors across all invocations; description quality is non-negotiable

dominance_rules.rule: Multi-agent handoff error visibility dominates pipeline throughput
dominance_rules.condition: error in upstream agent would be silently swallowed to maintain pipeline flow
dominance_rules.rationale: Silent error propagation in multi-agent chains causes cascading failure with no recovery signal

dominance_rules.rule: Memory write sanitization dominates memory persistence performance
dominance_rules.condition: raw unsanitized tool output would be written to shared memory store
dominance_rules.rationale: Poisoned memory entry persists across sessions and scales adversarial impact to all future interactions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change tool schema after fine-tuning data is generated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Schema changes invalidate all generated tool-call demonstrations; data regeneration is expensive

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not add tools to registry without corresponding schema validation rules
anti_rework_rules.trigger: new tool deployment without schema spec
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Unvalidated tools allow malformed argument injection; retrofitting validation after deployment requires re-testing all callers

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not tune latency/cost settings before error handling is complete
anti_rework_rules.trigger: optimization work begins before error classification taxonomy is defined
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Caching or early termination on unhandled error paths silently amplifies failures

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run evaluation before removing eval queries from training data
anti_rework_rules.trigger: eval suite run on model trained on data containing eval queries
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Contaminated evaluation invalidates all metric numbers; re-cleaning and retraining required

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy code execution sandbox without completing security review
anti_rework_rules.trigger: sandbox deployment skips security sign-off to meet deadline
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Post-deployment security patches for sandbox escapes require emergency re-deployment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not implement parallel tool calls without explicit independence verification in planner
anti_rework_rules.trigger: parallel fan-out added for performance without planner independence check
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Silent race conditions in parallel calls are extremely hard to debug post-deployment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not hard-code tool lists in agent; always use registry
anti_rework_rules.trigger: tool list embedded in agent code for convenience
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Hard-coded lists become stale and require code deployments for every tool registry change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not inject raw tool results without truncation and citation policy
anti_rework_rules.trigger: raw API response injected directly into context without formatting
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Raw injection wastes context budget and can include injected content from external sources

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize permission policy without multi-step privilege escalation audit
anti_rework_rules.trigger: single-tool permission check approved without checking tool-chaining combinations
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Individual tool permissions may be safe but combinations enable privilege escalation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy observability dashboards without testing alert thresholds on synthetic failures
anti_rework_rules.trigger: dashboards deployed without injected failure validation
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Untested alert thresholds either alert-fatigue or miss real incidents silently

iteration_protocol.trigger: new tool type added to registry
iteration_protocol.action: create schema, register with capability tags, add validation rules, update template if context budget allows
bump major version; freeze current training data; regenerate demonstrations post-schema; retrain

iteration_protocol.trigger: tool selection accuracy drops below 85% on evaluation
iteration_protocol.action: audit routing errors; identify schema ambiguity; add targeted demonstrations; re-evaluate

iteration_protocol.trigger: security vulnerability discovered in sandbox or permission model
iteration_protocol.action: emergency patch sandbox runtime; tighten permission policy; re-run security audit golden tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: ReAct loop latency exceeds P99 SLA
iteration_protocol.action: profile loop steps; identify parallelization opportunities; add result caching; re-benchmark

iteration_protocol.trigger: eval contamination detected in training data
iteration_protocol.action: deduplicate training data against eval by query hash; retrain; re-evaluate on clean holdout
add explicit status field to handoff schema; instrument inter-agent boundaries; load test
revoke compromised memory entries; add sanitization layer to all write paths; audit session scope policies

iteration_protocol.trigger: new LLM model with different tool-call format released
iteration_protocol.action: map new format to schema; update templates; assess whether fine-tuning data needs reformatting; re-evaluate

priority_rationale: Security and schema correctness first (trust boundary, schema design, validation, sandbox); core reasoning and routing next (ReAct, selection, planning, error handling); training pipeline after infrastructure (finetune, eval, self-supervised); operational concerns last (latency, observability, registry, templates, fallback).
